absent: Thresholds and margins used by fits_capacity and platform capacity scaling, plus pressure composition beyond hardware and frequency terms.
Numeric values and tuning of capacity scale, migrate break, pinned interval, migrate count, and idleness and migration type enumerations.
Contracts of load average refresh helpers, group share updates, idle clock handling, and frequency utilization notification.
Source selection, eligibility, detach and attach, migration feasibility, active balance stop routine, and imbalance accounting used by domain balance.
Full layouts of runqueue, fair queue, scheduling entity, group state, domain, group, and balance environment, plus locking for leaf list mutation.
Conditions selecting alternate builds for hardware load, interrupt utilization, blocked bookkeeping, leaf iteration, and hierarchical load.

findings.text: Task fit evaluation has three outcomes: fits, does not fit, or fits but boosted beyond present headroom. Without clamp usage only effective capacity matters. With clamps, architectural capacity governs clamp comparisons while effective capacity governs raw utilization, a maximum clamp can force fit except at top capacity, and an over minimum boosted task yields a distinct negative signal.

Effective capacity comes from stored per processor runqueue capacity, architectural capacity comes from platform scaling, and actual capacity for boost validation subtracts the larger of hardware load and frequency pressure from architectural capacity.
Fallback effective clamp is neutral: minimum requests no boost and maximum permits full scale.

Hierarchical task load is entity load scaled by ancestor chain share with a rounding guard and refreshed through a dated hierarchical pass; an alternate configuration reports entity load directly without hierarchy.

Hierarchical load refresh is idempotent within the same tick, builds an upward chain to the first fresh ancestor, seeds the top from its own average when reaching the root, then walks downward scaling parent load by child share.
Load tracking state carries separate sums and averages for load, utilization and runnability, with averages expected to vanish once sums vanish.

Runqueue state observed includes per class utilization averages, hardware load average, stored capacity, blocked load bookkeeping, and leaf fair queue list with scratch branch pointer, while fair queue state includes weight, averages, hierarchical load cache with timestamp and chaining link, queue count, propagation flag and parent contribution.
Fair queue to parent entity mapping yields absence for the root group and the owning group entity otherwise.
Blocked decay pass stamps the tick, refreshes non fair classes before fair, records whether any blocked load remains, and notifies frequency utilization only when something decayed.
Non fair blocked presence is true when any of realtime, deadline, hardware or interrupt utilization is nonzero; an alternate build always reports absence.

Realtime and deadline utilization expose stored runqueue averages, while hardware load and interrupt utilization each have an enabled accessor exposing a stored average and a disabled accessor fixed at zero.

Full fair blocked refresh walks leaf queues bottom up, refreshes each average and group share, idles the clock for empty queues, propagates eligible changes to the parent, drops fully decayed leaves, and reports incompleteness while load or utilization remains; a simplified build refreshes only the root queue.

A fully decayed fair queue requires zero weight, decayed average state, no queued child branch, and zero parent contribution; decayed average state requires all sums zero and expects averages zero; blocked load presence requires nonzero load or utilization average with an alternate always false build; parent propagation is skipped when entity averages are zero and no propagation is pending.
One build stamps the blocked refresh tick and clears the blocked flag when no blocked load remains, while an alternate build treats both operations as no operation.
Domain level pull balance attempts to move load toward the calling processor for a given idleness class and reports the amount moved, with a caller supplied continuation flag.

Balance proceeds through eligibility, optional domain serialization, source group and source queue selection, iterative detach and attach with break resumption, redirection to an alternate destination when pinned, same level retry after excluding a fully pinned source, failure accounting, conditional active balance kick, and interval backoff or reset.

Serialized domains admit at most one balancer through an acquire attempt and release store, the source queue is locked with interrupts saved across clock update and detach then released before attach with flags restored, and the active balance decision takes the source queue lock under interrupt disable with preemption controlled around the stopper kick.
Hierarchical load timestamp and chain links plus blocked tick and utilization averages use single read and write accessors suited to concurrent observation without heavier locking.

Active balance is not requested when the destination is outside current task affinity, when a balance is already pending, or when the current task already left the runqueue, and double setting of pending state is avoided under lock.

Fully pinned iterations must exclude the source and only retry when candidates outside the destination group remain, a parent imbalance marker is set on affinity failure and cleared on later success, and failure count plus interval backoff suppress newly idle, misfit and locality pinned cases to avoid excess migration.
Leaf iteration visits safe list membership in the grouped build and visits only the root queue in the non grouped build.

Child branch detection inspects the predecessor on the leaf list or scratch branch and reports a child when the predecessor parent group equals the queried group, with an empty list reporting absence.
